text:
alex: Evening handoff — quick snapshot.

What I did: saw p95/p99 regen latency spike in eu-west1 starting ~21:06 UTC, investigated routing and k8s pod restarts. Scaled regen pool to 6, temporarily enabled fallback routing to us-west for critical customers.

Blockers: intermittent `kvcache-evict` errors on some nodes causing cache misses and higher token generation time. Logs show repeated `timeout waiting for lock` on node-4.

Today / next: monitor latency for 30-45m, watch autoscaler, keep non-critical batch ingests paused (see below). If p95 stays > 2s for 3 consecutive 5m windows escalate.

oncall-bot: ALERT: regen-api eu-west1 p99 latency 7.2s at 21:06 UTC — triggered scaling policy.

mira: Took action — bumped node pool to 6 and cordoned node-4. p95 dropped ~35% after new pods came up. Will keep drains in progress.

sam: I'll tail logs and force-delete any CrashLoop pods. Command I'm running: 
```
kubectl get pods -n inference | grep regen
kubectl logs -f pod/regen-abcdef -n inference
kubectl delete pod regen-abcdef -n inference --grace-period=0 --force
```

alex: Routed traffic for customers [acct-1123, acct-998] to us-west via routing policy `fallback-eu->usw` (temporary). Added note in runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/regen-eu-fallback

toni: Paused non-critical batch-ingest jobs for the next 1h to reduce load. :pause_button:

deploy-bot: Deploy completed: hotfix/regen-timeout #432 merged to prod (22:02 UTC)

mira: @sam can you check the `kvcache-evict` stack traces? I saw repeated `panic: lease not found` entries.

sam: On it. Quick grep I ran:
```
kubectl logs -n inference pod/regen-xyz | grep kvcache-evict | tail -n 50
```
Found 24 matches with `timeout waiting for lock` between 21:05-21:12 UTC. Will attach snippets to INC-2024.

alex: Next steps: monitor p50/p95 for 30m, if regressions re-open full rollback plan. Created ticket INC-2024 and assigned to eng-oncall. I'm offline at 23:00 UTC — @mira please own nightwatch and escalate to SRE if autoscaler fails. ack :wave:
